_meta.method: complete direct literal rendering; source order preserved; no explanatory paraphrase

41.translation: Objection: if all action, causal factors, fruits, and so forth, and also every class of living being, are composed of the three guṇas, then how is liberation possible for this person? In answer: by worship of the Supreme Lord through actions enjoined according to one’s own eligibility, and by knowledge obtained through His grace. Thus, gathering and displaying the essence of the meaning of the entire Gītā, he begins another section, from ‘brāhmaṇas’ up to the end of the chapter. O scorcher of enemies: the actions of brāhmaṇas, kṣatriyas, vaiśyas, and śūdras are distinctly divided, strongly enjoined according to division. The separate mention of śūdras from ‘nature’ is because of their distinctness through absence of twice-born status. He gives an indication of the division: the qualities by which nature—sattvic and so forth—arises, becomes manifest, are the guṇas serving as indicators. Or the meaning is: they arise from nature, the impressions from a previous birth. There, brāhmaṇas have sattva predominant; kṣatriyas have rajas predominant with sattva subordinate; vaiśyas have rajas predominant with tamas subordinate; śūdras have tamas predominant with rajas subordinate.
word_for_word: nanu ca yadi evaṃ sarvam api kriyā-kāraka-phala-ādikaṃ prāṇi-jātaṃ ca triguṇa-ātmakam eva
objection: if all action, causal factors, fruits, and so forth, and also every class of living being, are composed of the three guṇas
kathaṃ tarhi asya mokṣaḥ iti apekṣāyām
then how is liberation possible for this person?
sva-sva-adhikāra-vihitaiḥ karmabhiḥ parameśvara-ārādhanāt
by worship of the Supreme Lord through actions enjoined according to one’s own eligibility
tat-prasāda-labdha-jñānena iti evaṃ
and by knowledge obtained through His grace
sarva-gītārtha-sāraṃ saṃgṛhya pradarśayituṃ prakaraṇa-antaram ārabhate
thus, gathering and displaying the essence of the meaning of the entire Gītā, he begins another section
brāhmaṇa-ity-ādi yāvat adhyāya-samāpti
from ‘brāhmaṇas’ up to the end of the chapter
he paraṃtapa śatru-tāpana
O scorcher of enemies
brāhmaṇānāṃ kṣatriyāṇāṃ viśāṃ ca śūdrāṇāṃ ca karmāṇi
the actions of brāhmaṇas, kṣatriyas, vaiśyas, and śūdras
pravibhaktāni prakarṣeṇa vibhāgataḥ vihitāni
are distinctly divided, strongly enjoined according to division
śūdrāṇāṃ svabhāvāt pṛthak-karaṇaṃ dvijatva-abhāvena vailakṣaṇyāt
the separate mention of śūdras from ‘nature’ is because of their distinctness through absence of twice-born status
vibhāga-upalakṣaṇam āha — svabhāvaḥ sāttvika-ādiḥ prabhavati prādurbhavati yebhyaḥ taiḥ guṇaiḥ upalakṣaṇa-bhūtaiḥ
he gives an indication of the division: the qualities by which nature—sattvic and so forth—arises, becomes manifest, are the guṇas serving as indicators
yad vā svabhāvaḥ pūrva-janma-saṃskāraḥ tasmāt prādurbhūtaiḥ iti arthaḥ
or the meaning is: they arise from nature, the impressions from a previous birth
tatra sattva-pradhānā brāhmaṇāḥ
there, brāhmaṇas have sattva predominant
sattva-upasarjana-rajaḥ-pradhānāḥ kṣatriyāḥ
kṣatriyas have rajas predominant with sattva subordinate
tama-upasarjana-rajaḥ-pradhānā vaiśyāḥ
vaiśyas have rajas predominant with tamas subordinate
raja-upasarjana-tamaḥ-pradhānāḥ śūdrāḥ
śūdras have tamas predominant with rajas subordinate

42.translation: There he states the natural actions of a brāhmaṇa with ‘tranquility.’ Tranquility is cessation of the mind. Restraint is cessation of the external senses. Austerity is the bodily and other austerity stated earlier. Purity is external and internal. Forbearance is forgiveness. Straightforwardness is absence of crookedness. Knowledge is scriptural. Realization is experience. Āstikya is the certainty ‘there is a world hereafter.’ This group beginning with tranquility is action born from the nature of a brāhmaṇa.
word_for_word: tatra brāhmaṇasya svābhāvikāni karmāṇi āha — śama iti
there he states the natural actions of a brāhmaṇa with ‘tranquility’
śamaḥ citta-uparamaḥ
tranquility is cessation of the mind
damaḥ bāhya-indriya-uparamaḥ
restraint is cessation of the external senses
tapaḥ pūrvoktaṃ śārīra-ādi
austerity is the bodily and other austerity stated earlier
śaucaṃ bāhya-abhyantaram
purity is external and internal
kṣāntiḥ kṣamā
forbearance is forgiveness
ārjavam avakratā
straightforwardness is absence of crookedness
jñānaṃ śāstrīyam
knowledge is scriptural
vijñānam anubhavaḥ
realization is experience
āstikyam asti para-loka iti niścayaḥ
āstikya is the certainty ‘there is a world hereafter’
etat śama-ādi brāhmaṇasya svabhāvāt jātaṃ karma
this group beginning with tranquility is action born from the nature of a brāhmaṇa

43.translation: He states the natural actions of a kṣatriya with ‘heroism.’ Heroism is valor. Vigor is boldness. Fortitude is courage. Skill is competence. Not fleeing in battle is not turning one’s back. Gift is generosity. Lordly disposition is the power to govern. This is action born from the nature of a kṣatriya.
word_for_word: kṣatriyasya svābhāvikāni karmāṇi āha — śauryam iti
he states the natural actions of a kṣatriya with ‘heroism’
śauryaṃ parākramaḥ
heroism is valor
tejaḥ prāgalbhyam
vigor is boldness
dhṛtiḥ dhairyam
fortitude is courage
dākṣyaṃ kauśalam
skill is competence
yuddhe ca api apalāyanam parāṅmukhatā-abhāvaḥ
not fleeing in battle is not turning one’s back
dānam audāryam
gift is generosity
īśvara-bhāvaḥ niyamana-śaktiḥ
lordly disposition is the power to govern
etat kṣatriyasya svabhāva-jaṃ karma
this is action born from the nature of a kṣatriya

44.translation: He states the actions of vaiśyas and śūdras with ‘agriculture.’ Agriculture is ploughing. One who protects cows is a cow-protector; the state of that is cow-protection, meaning tending cattle. Trade is buying and selling and so forth. This is action born from the nature of a vaiśya. Service whose nature is attendance on the three varṇas is also action born from the nature of a śūdra.
word_for_word: vaiśya-śūdrayoḥ karma āha — kṛṣi iti
he states the actions of vaiśyas and śūdras with ‘agriculture’
kṛṣiḥ karṣaṇam
agriculture is ploughing
gāḥ rakṣati iti go-rakṣaḥ tasya bhāvo go-rakṣyam
one who protects cows is a cow-protector; the state of that is cow-protection
pāśu-pālyam iti arthaḥ
meaning tending cattle
vāṇijyaṃ kraya-vikraya-ādi
trade is buying and selling and so forth
etat vaiśyasya svabhāva-jaṃ karma
this is action born from the nature of a vaiśya
trai-varṇika-paricaryā-ātmakaṃ śūdrasya api svabhāva-jaṃ karma
service whose nature is attendance on the three varṇas is also action born from the nature of a śūdra

45.translation: Objection: then, for one who has the conceit ‘I act,’ the stain of action is unavoidable; because his mind is impure, renunciation also does not exist. A great difficulty has arisen. Anticipating this, he says ‘in Brahman.’ One who, placing actions in Brahman, offering them to the Supreme Lord, and abandoning attachment to their fruit, performs actions, is not smeared by action consisting of merit and demerit, which is most sinful in being a cause of bondage. Just as a lotus leaf, though situated in water, is not smeared by water, so too this person.
word_for_word: tarhi yasya karomi iti abhimāno asti tasya karma-lepo durvāraḥ
objection: then, for one who has the conceit ‘I act,’ the stain of action is unavoidable
aviśuddha-cittatvāt saṃnyāso api na asti iti mahat saṃkaṭam āpannam iti āśaṅkya āha brahmaṇi iti
because his mind is impure, renunciation also does not exist; a great difficulty has arisen; anticipating this, he says ‘in Brahman’
brahmaṇi ādhāya parameśvare samarpya
placing actions in Brahman, offering them to the Supreme Lord
tat-phale ca saṅgaṃ tyaktvā yaḥ karmāṇi karoti
and abandoning attachment to their fruit, one who performs actions
asau pāpena bandha-hetutayā pāpiṣṭhena puṇya-pāpa-ātmakena karmaṇā na lipyate
is not smeared by action consisting of merit and demerit, which is most sinful in being a cause of bondage
yathā padma-patram ambhasi sthitam api ambhasā na lipyate tadvat
just as a lotus leaf, though situated in water, is not smeared by water, so too this person

46.translation: He states that very point with ‘from whom.’ From the Supreme Lord, the inner ruler, arises the activity, the movement, of beings. And by Him, as the causal Self, this entire universe is spread, pervaded. Worshipping, honoring, that Lord through one’s own action, a person attains perfection.
word_for_word: tam eva āha — yata iti
he states that very point with ‘from whom’
yataḥ antaryāmiṇaḥ parameśvarāt bhūtānāṃ prāṇināṃ pravṛttiḥ ceṣṭā bhavati
from the Supreme Lord, the inner ruler, arises the activity, the movement, of beings
yena ca kāraṇa-ātmanā sarvam idaṃ viśvaṃ tatam vyāptam
and by Him, as the causal Self, this entire universe is spread, pervaded
tam īśvaraṃ sva-karmaṇā abhyarcya pūjayitvā
worshipping, honoring, that Lord through one’s own action
siddhiṃ labhate manuṣyaḥ
a person attains perfection

47.translation: He states the result of the qualification ‘through one’s own action’ with ‘better.’ One’s own dharma, even without its full qualities, is better, superior, to another’s dharma even when well performed. And it should not be thought that another’s dharma such as begging is better than one’s own dharma such as battle, which includes killing relatives and the like. For, performing the action prescribed, laid down, by the previously stated nature, one does not incur sin.
word_for_word: sva-karmaṇā iti viśeṣaṇasya phalam āha — śreyān iti
he states the result of the qualification ‘through one’s own action’ with ‘better’
viguṇaḥ api sva-dharmaḥ samyak-anuṣṭhitāt api para-dharmāt śreyān śreṣṭhaḥ
one’s own dharma, even without its full qualities, is better, superior, to another’s dharma even when well performed
na ca bandhu-vadha-ādi-yuktāt yuddha-ādeḥ sva-dharmāt bhikṣāṭana-ādi-para-dharmaḥ śreṣṭha iti mantavyam
and it should not be thought that another’s dharma such as begging is better than one’s own dharma such as battle, which includes killing relatives and the like
yataḥ svabhāvena pūrvoktena niyataṃ niyamena uktaṃ karma kurvan
for, performing the action prescribed, laid down, by the previously stated nature
kilbiṣaṃ na āpnoti
one does not incur sin

48.translation: If, again, from the Sāṅkhya standpoint, considering the fault characterized by violence in one’s own dharma, you regard another’s dharma as better, then faultiness is equal in the other dharma also. With this intention he says ‘natural.’ One should not abandon action enjoined by one’s nature, even though it has fault. For all undertakings whatsoever, for visible or unseen ends, are indeed covered, pervaded, by some fault, just as fire is covered by naturally arising smoke. Therefore, just as, removing the fault in the form of smoke from fire, its heat alone is used to remove darkness, cold, and so forth, so also, leaving aside the faulty portion of action, only its good portion is to be used for purity of sattva. This is the meaning.
word_for_word: yadi punaḥ sāṃkhya-dṛṣṭyā sva-dharme hiṃsā-lakṣaṇaṃ doṣaṃ matvā para-dharmaṃ śreṣṭhaṃ manyase
if, again, from the Sāṅkhya standpoint, considering the fault characterized by violence in one’s own dharma, you regard another’s dharma as better
tarhi sa-doṣatvaṃ para-dharme api tulyam iti āśayena āha — sahajam iti
then faultiness is equal in the other dharma also; with this intention he says ‘natural’
sahajaṃ svabhāva-vihitaṃ karma sa-doṣam api na tyajet
one should not abandon action enjoined by one’s nature, even though it has fault
hi yasmāt sarve api ārambhā dṛṣṭa-adṛṣṭa-arthāni sarvāṇi api karmāṇi
for all undertakings whatsoever, for visible or unseen ends
doṣeṇa kenacid āvṛtā vyāptā eva
are indeed covered, pervaded, by some fault
yathā sahajena dhūmena agniḥ āvṛtaḥ tadvat
just as fire is covered by naturally arising smoke
ataḥ yathā agneḥ dhūma-rūpaṃ doṣam apākṛtya pratāpa eva tamaḥ-śīta-ādi-nivṛttaye sevyate
therefore, just as, removing the fault in the form of smoke from fire, its heat alone is used to remove darkness, cold, and so forth
tathā karmaṇaḥ api doṣa-aṃśaṃ vihāya guṇa-aṃśa eva sattva-śuddhaye sevyate
so also, leaving aside the faulty portion of action, only its good portion is to be used for purity of sattva
iti arthaḥ
this is the meaning

49.translation: Objection: while action is being performed, how will only the good portion be obtained through abandoning the faulty portion? In answer he says ‘unattached.’ One whose intellect is unattached, devoid of attachment; who has conquered the self, without ego; whose longing has departed, whose desire for fruit has gone: by renunciation of such a kind—the previously stated sattvic relinquishment characterized by abandoning attachment to action and its fruit—one attains the perfection of actionlessness, purity of sattva characterized by cessation of all action. Although performance of action with abandonment of attachment and fruit is itself actionlessness, because there is no insistence on doership—as stated in the four verses beginning ‘the knower of truth, disciplined, should think: I do nothing at all’—nevertheless by renunciation of the stated character one attains supreme perfection of actionlessness, characterized by ‘having mentally renounced all actions, the self-controlled one sits happily,’ otherwise called the state of the paramahaṃsa.
word_for_word: nanu kathaṃ karmaṇi kriyamāṇe doṣa-aṃśa-prahāṇena guṇa-aṃśa eva saṃpatsyate iti apekṣāyām āha — asakta iti
objection: while action is being performed, how will only the good portion be obtained through abandoning the faulty portion? in answer he says ‘unattached’
asaktā saṅga-śūnyā buddhiḥ yasya
one whose intellect is unattached, devoid of attachment
jita-ātmā nirahaṅkāraḥ
who has conquered the self, without ego
vigata-spṛhaḥ vigatā spṛhā phala-viṣaya-icchā yasmāt
whose longing has departed, whose desire for fruit has gone
sa evaṃ-bhūtena sa tyāgaḥ sāttviko mata iti evaṃ pūrvoktena
by such previously stated sattvic relinquishment
karma-āsakti-tat-phalayoḥ tyāga-lakṣaṇena saṃnyāsena
by renunciation characterized by abandoning attachment to action and its fruit
naiṣkarmya-siddhiṃ sarva-karma-nivṛtti-lakṣaṇāṃ sattva-śuddhim adhigacchati
one attains the perfection of actionlessness, purity of sattva characterized by cessation of all action
yady api saṅga-phalayoḥ tyāgena karma-anuṣṭhānam api naiṣkarmyam eva
although performance of action with abandonment of attachment and fruit is itself actionlessness
kartṛtva-abhiniveśa-abhāvāt
because there is no insistence on doership
tad uktam — na eva kiṃcit karomi iti yukto manyeta tattvavit ity-ādi-śloka-catuṣṭayena
as stated in the four verses beginning ‘the knower of truth, disciplined, should think: I do nothing at all’
tathā api anena ukta-lakṣaṇena saṃnyāsena paramāṃ naiṣkarmya-siddhim
nevertheless by renunciation of the stated character one attains supreme perfection of actionlessness
sarva-karmāṇi manasā saṃnyasya āste sukhaṃ vaśī iti evaṃ-lakṣaṇām
characterized by ‘having mentally renounced all actions, the self-controlled one sits happily’
pāramahaṃsya-apara-paryāyāṃ prāpnoti
otherwise called the state of the paramahaṃsa

50.translation: He states, in six verses beginning ‘having attained perfection,’ the manner in which such a paramahaṃsa, through steadfastness in knowledge, comes to the state of Brahman. Having attained the perfection of actionlessness, by what manner one attains Brahman—understand that manner from My statement, in brief only.
word_for_word: evaṃ-bhūtasya paramahaṃsasya jñāna-niṣṭhayā brahma-bhāva-prakāram āha — siddhiṃ prāpta iti ṣaḍbhiḥ
he states, in six verses beginning ‘having attained perfection,’ the manner in which such a paramahaṃsa, through steadfastness in knowledge, comes to the state of Brahman
naiṣkarmya-siddhiṃ prāptaḥ san
having attained the perfection of actionlessness
yathā yena prakāreṇa brahma prāpnoti
by what manner one attains Brahman
tathā taṃ prakāraṃ saṃkṣepeṇa eva me vacanāt nibodha
understand that manner from My statement, in brief only

51.translation: He states that with ‘by intellect.’ Endowed with the purified, previously stated sattvic intellect in the manner described; by sattvic fortitude restraining the self, that very intellect, making it unmoving; abandoning objects beginning with sound; casting away attraction and aversion toward those objects—the construction of ‘endowed with purified intellect’ and the other expressions continues to ‘becomes fit for the state of Brahman’ in the third verse.
word_for_word: tad eva āha — buddhyā iti
he states that with ‘by intellect’
uktena prakāreṇa viśuddhayā pūrvoktayā sāttvikyā buddhyā yuktaḥ
endowed with the purified, previously stated sattvic intellect in the manner described
dhṛtyā sāttvikyā ātmānaṃ tām eva buddhiṃ niyamya niścalāṃ kṛtvā
by sattvic fortitude restraining the self, that very intellect, making it unmoving
śabda-ādīn viṣayān tyaktvā
abandoning objects beginning with sound
tad-viṣayau rāga-dveṣau ca vyudasya
casting away attraction and aversion toward those objects
buddhyā viśuddhayā yuktaḥ ity-ādīnām brahma-bhūyāya kalpate iti tṛtīyena anvayaḥ
the construction of ‘endowed with purified intellect’ and the other expressions continues to ‘becomes fit for the state of Brahman’ in the third verse

52.translation: And further, with ‘frequenting solitude.’ One who frequents solitude, residing in a pure place; eating lightly, eating moderately; by these means becoming restrained in speech, body, and mind; always, at all times, devoted to that yoga through meditation which is contact with Brahman; and, for uninterrupted meditation, repeatedly taking complete refuge in firm dispassion.
word_for_word: kiṃ ca — vivikta iti
and further, with ‘frequenting solitude’
vivikta-sevī śuddha-deśa-avasthāyī
one who frequents solitude, residing in a pure place
laghv-āśī mita-bhojī
eating lightly, eating moderately
etaiḥ upāyaiḥ yata-vāk-kāya-mānasaḥ saṃyata-vāg-deha-cittaḥ bhūtvā
by these means becoming restrained in speech, body, and mind
nityaṃ sarvadā dhyānena yo yogo brahma-saṃsparśaḥ tat-paraḥ san
always, at all times, devoted to that yoga through meditation which is contact with Brahman
dhyāna-aviccheda-arthaṃ punaḥ punaḥ dṛḍhaṃ vairāgyaṃ samyak upāśritaḥ bhūtvā
and, for uninterrupted meditation, repeatedly taking complete refuge in firm dispassion

53.translation: And further, with ‘ego.’ Then abandoning especially ego such as ‘I am detached,’ force meaning obstinate insistence, pride characterized by going astray through the power of yoga, desire and anger even toward objects obtained under the force of begun karma, and possession; being without ‘mine’ regarding things that come forcibly; peaceful, having attained supreme quietude; he becomes fit for the state of Brahman, for remaining steadily in the certainty ‘I am Brahman.’
word_for_word: kiṃ ca — ahaṅkāram iti
and further, with ‘ego’
tataḥ ca viraktaḥ aham ity-ādi-ahaṅkāraṃ
then ego such as ‘I am detached’
balaṃ durāgraham
force meaning obstinate insistence
darpaṃ yoga-balāt unmārga-pravṛtti-lakṣaṇam
pride characterized by going astray through the power of yoga
prārabdha-vaśāt prāpyamāṇeṣu api viṣayeṣu kāmaṃ krodham
desire and anger even toward objects obtained under the force of begun karma
parigrahaṃ ca vimucya viśeṣeṇa tyaktvā
and possession, abandoning them especially
balāt āpanneṣu nirmamaḥ san
being without ‘mine’ regarding things that come forcibly
śāntaḥ parām upaśāntiṃ prāptaḥ
peaceful, having attained supreme quietude
brahma-bhūyāya brahma aham iti naiścalyena avasthānāya kalpate yogyo bhavati
he becomes fit for the state of Brahman, for remaining steadily in the certainty ‘I am Brahman’

54.translation: He states the fruit of remaining steadily in the certainty ‘I am Brahman’ with ‘become Brahman.’ Become Brahman means established in Brahman. With a serene mind, he does not grieve for what has been lost, nor does he desire what has not been obtained, because identification with body and the rest is absent. Therefore, being equal toward all beings, because distraction caused by attraction, aversion, and the rest is absent, he obtains supreme devotion to Me characterized by seeing My being in all beings.
word_for_word: brahma aham iti evaṃ naiścalyena avasthānasya phalam āha — brahma-bhūta iti
he states the fruit of remaining steadily in the certainty ‘I am Brahman’ with ‘become Brahman’
brahma-bhūtaḥ brahmaṇi avasthitaḥ
become Brahman means established in Brahman
prasanna-cittaḥ naṣṭaṃ na śocati
with a serene mind, he does not grieve for what has been lost
na ca aprāptaṃ kāṅkṣati deha-ādi-abhimāna-abhāvāt
nor does he desire what has not been obtained, because identification with body and the rest is absent
ata eva sarveṣu api bhūteṣu samaḥ san
therefore, being equal toward all beings
rāga-dveṣa-ādi-kṛta-vikṣepa-abhāvāt
because distraction caused by attraction, aversion, and the rest is absent
sarva-bhūteṣu mad-bhāvanā-lakṣaṇāṃ parāṃ mad-bhaktiṃ labhate
he obtains supreme devotion to Me characterized by seeing My being in all beings

55.translation: Then, with ‘through devotion.’ Through that supreme devotion he knows Me in truth. Of what kind? How great I am—all-pervading—and who I am, a compact mass of existence, consciousness, and bliss. Then, having thus known Me in truth, afterward, when even that knowledge has subsided, he enters Me. The meaning is: he becomes of the nature of supreme bliss.
word_for_word: tataḥ ca — bhaktyā mām iti
then, with ‘through devotion’
tayā ca parayā bhaktyā tattvataḥ mām abhijānāti
through that supreme devotion he knows Me in truth
kathaṃ-bhūtam
of what kind?
yāvān sarva-vyāpī
how great I am—all-pervading
yaḥ ca asmi sat-cit-ānanda-ghanaḥ tathā-bhūtam
and who I am, a compact mass of existence, consciousness, and bliss
tataḥ ca mām evaṃ tattvataḥ jñātvā
then, having thus known Me in truth
tad-anantaraṃ tasya jñānasya api uparame sati māṃ viśate
afterward, when even that knowledge has subsided, he enters Me
paramānanda-rūpo bhavati iti arthaḥ
the meaning is: he becomes of the nature of supreme bliss

56.translation: He concludes the manner of liberation stated through worship of the Supreme Lord by one’s own actions with ‘all actions.’ Performing all actions—obligatory, occasional, and desire-motivated—in the previously stated order, taking Me as refuge, one whose refuge to be taken is I alone and not a fruit such as heaven, by My grace attains the eternal, beginningless, imperishable, everlasting, supremely excellent Vaiṣṇava state.
word_for_word: sva-karmabhiḥ parameśvara-ārādhanāt uktaṃ mokṣa-prakāram upasaṃharati — sarva-karmāṇi iti
he concludes the manner of liberation stated through worship of the Supreme Lord by one’s own actions with ‘all actions’
sarva-karmāṇi nitya-naimittikāni kāmyāni ca karmāṇi
all actions—obligatory, occasional, and desire-motivated
pūrvokta-krameṇa mad-vyapāśrayaḥ san kurvāṇaḥ
performing them in the previously stated order, taking Me as refuge
aham eva vyapāśrayaḥ āśrayaṇīyo na tu svarga-ādi-phalaṃ yasya saḥ
one whose refuge to be taken is I alone and not a fruit such as heaven
mat-prasādāt śāśvatam anādi avyayaṃ nityaṃ sarvotkṛṣṭaṃ vaiṣṇavaṃ padam prāpnoti
by My grace attains the eternal, beginningless, imperishable, everlasting, supremely excellent Vaiṣṇava state

57.translation: Because this is so, therefore with ‘by the mind.’ Mentally renouncing, offering, all actions in Me; one for whom I alone am the supreme end to be attained, the human goal; taking refuge in the yoga of resolute intellect; at all times, even during performance of action, by the principle ‘the offering is Brahman, the oblation is Brahman,’ become one whose mind is in Me alone.
word_for_word: yasmāt evaṃ tasmāt — cetasā iti
because this is so, therefore with ‘by the mind’
sarva-karmāṇi cetasā mayi saṃnyasya samarpya
mentally renouncing, offering, all actions in Me
mat-paraḥ aham eva paraḥ prāpyaḥ puruṣārtho yasya saḥ
one for whom I alone am the supreme end to be attained, the human goal
vyavasāya-ātmikayā buddhyā yogam āśritya
taking refuge in the yoga of resolute intellect
satataṃ karma-anuṣṭhāna-kāle api brahmārpaṇaṃ brahma-haviḥ iti nyāyena
at all times, even during performance of action, by the principle ‘the offering is Brahman, the oblation is Brahman’
mayi eva cittaṃ yasya tathā-bhūto bhava
become one whose mind is in Me alone

58.translation: Then hear what will happen, with ‘mind in Me.’ Being one whose mind is in Me, by My grace you will cross all difficulties, all hard-to-cross worldly sufferings. He states the fault on the opposite side: but if you, again, from ego—from the conceit of being the knower—do not listen to this stated by Me, then you will perish, fall away from the human goal.
word_for_word: tataḥ yat bhaviṣyati tat śṛṇu — mat-citta iti
then hear what will happen, with ‘mind in Me’
mat-cittaḥ san mat-prasādāt sarvāṇi api durgāṇi dustarāṇi sāṃsārikāṇi duḥkhāni tariṣyasi
being one whose mind is in Me, by My grace you will cross all difficulties, all hard-to-cross worldly sufferings
vipakṣe doṣam āha
he states the fault on the opposite side
atha cet yadi punaḥ tvam ahaṅkārāt jñātṛtva-abhimānāt
but if you, again, from ego—from the conceit of being the knower
mad-uktam etat na śroṣyasi
do not listen to this stated by Me
tarhi vinaṅkṣyasi puruṣārthāt bhraśyasi
then you will perish, fall away from the human goal

59.translation: If you say, ‘Let me perish; nevertheless I will not fight with my relatives,’ to this he says ‘that which.’ Disregarding what I have said and relying only on ego, the determination you make, thinking ‘I will not fight,’ is certainly false, because you are not independent. He states that very thing: your prakṛti, having transformed into the form of rajas, will appoint you, will certainly set you in motion in battle.
word_for_word: kāmaṃ vinaṅkṣyāmi na tu bandhubhiḥ yuddhaṃ kariṣyāmi iti cet
if you say, ‘let me perish; nevertheless I will not fight with my relatives’
tatra āha — yat iti
to this he says ‘that which’
mad-uktam anādṛtya kevalam ahaṅkāram avalambya yuddhaṃ na kariṣyāmi iti
disregarding what I have said and relying only on ego, thinking ‘I will not fight’
tvaṃ yat manyase adhyavasyasi eṣa te adhyavasāyo mithyā eva
the determination you make is certainly false
asvatantratvāt tava
because you are not independent
tad eva āha — prakṛtiḥ tvāṃ rajo-guṇa-rūpeṇa pariṇatā satī
he states that very thing: your prakṛti, having transformed into the form of rajas
niyokṣyati yuddhe pravartayiṣyati eva
will appoint you, will certainly set you in motion in battle

60.translation: And further, with ‘nature.’ Nature means the impressions from previous action that are the cause of kṣatriya-hood. Bound, constrained, by one’s own action born from that—heroism and the rest stated earlier—you do not wish, through delusion, to perform the action characterized by battle; yet, even powerless, you will certainly perform that action.
word_for_word: kiṃ ca — svabhāva iti
and further, with ‘nature’
svabhāvaḥ kṣatriyatve hetuḥ pūrva-karma-saṃskāraḥ
nature means the impressions from previous action that are the cause of kṣatriya-hood
tasmāt jātena svakīyena karmaṇā śaurya-ādinā pūrvoktena nibaddhaḥ yantritaḥ tvam
bound, constrained, by one’s own action born from that—heroism and the rest stated earlier
mohāt yat karma yuddha-lakṣaṇaṃ kartuṃ na icchasi
you do not wish, through delusion, to perform the action characterized by battle
avaśaḥ api tat karma kariṣyasi eva
yet, even powerless, you will certainly perform that action
